from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from pysat.formula import CNF
import itertools

n = 11
m = 2  # two copies
length = m * n  # 22

# We'll use variables: position p (0-indexed) gets value v (1..n)
# Variable index = p * n + v (1-indexed for pysat)
def var(p, v):
    return p * n + v + 1  # +1 because pysat uses 1-indexed

solver = Glucose3()

# Each position gets exactly one value
for p in range(length):
    clause = [var(p, v) for v in range(1, n+1)]
    solver.add_clause(clause)
    # At most one: pairwise negative
    for v1 in range(1, n+1):
        for v2 in range(v1+1, n+1):
            solver.add_clause([-var(p, v1), -var(p, v2)])

# Each value appears exactly twice
for v in range(1, n+1):
    # At least two occurrences
    # We'll encode exactly two by: at least two, at most two
    # At least two: for each pair of positions, ensure not all others are false... simpler: use at-most-two and at-least-two
    pass

# Actually let's use a different encoding: each value v appears exactly twice, with distance v+1
# So positions p and p+v+1 both get value v

# For each value v, we need to choose a starting position p such that p + v + 1 < length
# p from 0 to length - (v+1) - 1 = length - v - 2

# Exactly one starting position per value
for v in range(1, n+1):
    possible_starts = [p for p in range(length - v - 1)]  # p + v + 1 < length
    # At least one start
    solver.add_clause([var(p, v) for p in possible_starts])
    # At most one start: pairwise negative
    for i, p1 in enumerate(possible_starts):
        for p2 in possible_starts[i+1:]:
            solver.add_clause([-var(p1, v), -var(p2, v)])

# If position p gets value v, then position p+v+1 must also get value v
for v in range(1, n+1):
    for p in range(length - v - 1):
        # var(p, v) implies var(p+v+1, v)
        solver.add_clause([-var(p, v), var(p+v+1, v)])
        # var(p+v+1, v) implies var(p, v)
        solver.add_clause([var(p, v), -var(p+v+1, v)])

# Also ensure no position gets two values (already covered by at-most-one per position)

result = solver.solve()
print("Satisfiable:", result)

if result:
    model = solver.get_model()
    # Decode
    seq = [0] * length
    for p in range(length):
        for v in range(1, n+1):
            if model[var(p, v)-1] > 0:
                seq[p] = v
                break
    print("Sequence:", seq)
    # Verify
    for v in range(1, n+1):
        positions = [i for i, x in enumerate(seq) if x == v]
        print(f"Value {v}: positions {positions}, distance = {positions[1] - positions[0]}")
else:
    print("UNSATISFIABLE")
